newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NORMAN, DUVAL SHARE HALFWAY LEAD AT RAIN-SUSPENDED DORAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN, DUVAL SHARE HALFWAY LEAD AT RAIN-SUSPENDED DORAL.

text.p: Greg Norman and David Duval
shared the halfway lead in the rain-suspended Doral Open at
10-under-par 134 Friday with 15 players yet to complete the
second round.
Norman shot a second round of four-under-par 68 on the
Blue Monster course where he has won three times, while Duval,
wtill looking for his first career win, had a 66.
One stroke behind was the man in the passenger seat in
Norman's helicopter every morning this week, Zimbabwe's Nick
Price, whose 67 put him at nine under. Australian Steve
Elkington was next on the leaderboard, eight under after a 66.
Price was one of the last players to finish before the
round was suspended until Saturday morning.
A one-hour rain delay left 15 players with incomplete
rounds after play was called for darkness. The player with the
best score among the non-finishers was Doug Martin, who was
six under par with just one hole to play.
With the leaders theoretically halfway to a winning score
of 20 under par, the Raymond Floyd-directed renovation of the
Doral Blue course to its former level of difficulty seems to
be only a limited success.
"You have to give the players their due. Players get
better and better as each year goes by, no matter what golf
course you throw at them. Ask them to drive it up a gnat's
ass, and they'll drive it up a gnat's ass and make birdie --
that's how good they are," said Norman.
Norman had six birdies in his round, and two bogeys, both
from failing to get up and down from the sand. Except for a
two-putt from 18 feet on the par five first hole, all of
Norman's birdie putts were mid-range putts between 10 and 15
feet.
"I'm playing well now. I'm hitting shots I'm starting to
feel very comfortable with, and that's a nice feeling to
have," said Norman.
Duval, who equalled the low round of the day, last led a
tournament last month at Pebble Beach, where he topped the
leaderboard after three rounds but then picked up his sixth
career second-place finish.
His bogey-free second round here had six birdies, all but
one of them from putts inside eight feet. "I didn't hit the
ball well on the range or on the first couple of holes and hit
it in a lot of bunkers. Then I started driving better, hitting
it in the fairways, and it got a lot easier," said Duval.
Duval said that he is not frustrated about not winning,
nor with all the inevitable questions about when he finally
will win.
"If I wasn't asked about it, I'd feel like people didn't
think very highly of me as a player. Since I am asked all the
time it shows that a lot of people believe in my abilities,"
said Duval.
